notes: Root-key homograph: shares bare consonants חשך with already-shipped H2821 ("grow dark") -- Strong's own entry for H2820 even calls the two "interchangeable." Per the root-key superscript convention (lower Strong's number gets ¹), this root is חשך¹ and H2821 has been retroactively relabeled חשך² in this same batch.

That interchange is visible in the corpus itself, not just the lexicon cross-reference: H2821's own shipped citation for qal perfect 3ms (Ezek.30.18, חָשַׂ֣ךְ) is written with the *sin* dot -- orthographically identical to this root's spelling -- while H2821's other forms (e.g. Lam.5.17, חָשְׁכ֥וּ) carry the *shin* dot. The corpus's lemma tagging (2820 vs. 2821) still reliably separates the two roots' occurrences; flagging this only because it's a real, pre-existing orthographic wrinkle worth being aware of, not something this batch changed.

Qal gloss trimmed from the requested "withhold; restrain; spare" to "withhold; spare": "restrain" (e.g. Job.7.11 "I will not restrain my mouth," Jer.14.10 "they have not restrained their feet") is the same evidenced sense as "withhold" worded twice. "Spare" is genuinely distinct and independently attested at Prov.13.24 ("he who spares his rod hates his son") -- a different action (declining to apply/use something) from "withhold" (declining to give/release something), so both clauses stay.

Niphal gloss trimmed from the requested "be assuaged; be spared" to "be assuaged": the corpus has two occurrences of this exact slot (niphal yiqtol 3ms) -- Job.16.6 (יֵחָשֵׂךְ, "assuaged," pain not lessened) and Job.21.30 (יֵחָשֶׂךְ, arguably "is spared/reserved," of the wicked kept for a day of calamity). Both are real, but they occupy the identical morphological slot, so only one can be the stored citation (Job.16.6, per the standard tie-break) -- shipping "be spared" as a second clause would leave it without a citation actually visible in this root's data. Flagging Job.21.30's alternate reading here rather than silently dropping it.
